title: Recursion Basics — Call, Pause, Return
code: public static int SumPrefix(int[] nums, int count)
if (count == 0) return 0;                      // BASE: no items remain
int smaller = SumPrefix(nums, count - 1);      // PROGRESS + recursive call
return smaller + nums[count - 1];             // RESUME: finish this call's work

nums.label: Input — active call owns the highlighted prefix

calls.label: Live calls — count values; top (active call) at right

pending.label: Paused callers — addition still to finish

frames.caption: Sum [3, 1, 4, 2]. Watch each call stop, delegate, or resume.
frames.note: Each call promises to sum the first count items. Blue marks the active call; the pending-work board records paused callers. Numbers in the stack are count arguments, not answers. Nothing has been called yet.

frames.caption: ENTER count=4: this call owns 4 item(s).
frames.note: A call creates a new frame with its own count and a place for its smaller answer. Older frames stay live. The current call checks the base case before delegating.

frames.caption: PAUSE count=4: ask count=3; save “child answer + 2”.
frames.note: count - 1 guarantees progress toward zero. The caller cannot add yet: smaller is unknown until the child returns. The array stays unchanged; the child simply owns a shorter prefix.

frames.caption: ENTER count=3: this call owns 3 item(s).
frames.note: A call creates a new frame with its own count and a place for its smaller answer. Older frames stay live. The current call checks the base case before delegating.

frames.caption: PAUSE count=3: ask count=2; save “child answer + 4”.
frames.note: count - 1 guarantees progress toward zero. The caller cannot add yet: smaller is unknown until the child returns. The array stays unchanged; the child simply owns a shorter prefix.

frames.caption: ENTER count=2: this call owns 2 item(s).
frames.note: A call creates a new frame with its own count and a place for its smaller answer. Older frames stay live. The current call checks the base case before delegating.

frames.caption: PAUSE count=2: ask count=1; save “child answer + 1”.
frames.note: count - 1 guarantees progress toward zero. The caller cannot add yet: smaller is unknown until the child returns. The array stays unchanged; the child simply owns a shorter prefix.

frames.caption: ENTER count=1: this call owns 1 item(s).
frames.note: A call creates a new frame with its own count and a place for its smaller answer. Older frames stay live. The current call checks the base case before delegating.

frames.caption: PAUSE count=1: ask count=0; save “child answer + 3”.
frames.note: count - 1 guarantees progress toward zero. The caller cannot add yet: smaller is unknown until the child returns. The array stays unchanged; the child simply owns a shorter prefix.

frames.caption: ENTER count=0: this call owns 0 item(s).
frames.note: A call creates a new frame with its own count and a place for its smaller answer. Older frames stay live. The current call checks the base case before delegating.

frames.caption: BASE CASE: the empty prefix returns 0. No further call.
frames.note: The base case supplies a known answer without recursion. It ends this call only: the other four frames are paused and still have additions to finish. This is the deepest point: five live frames.

frames.caption: RESUME count=1: the child returned 0; assign smaller=0.
frames.note: The child frame has left the stack. Execution continues in its immediate caller at the suspended assignment; it does not jump straight to the first call. This caller still has its own addition to do.

frames.caption: RETURN count=1: 0 + 3 = 3.
frames.note: Finish this frame’s pending work, then return its answer to the next caller. Answers flow back in reverse call order because the most recent unfinished caller resumes first.

frames.caption: RESUME count=2: the child returned 3; assign smaller=3.
frames.note: The child frame has left the stack. Execution continues in its immediate caller at the suspended assignment; it does not jump straight to the first call. This caller still has its own addition to do.

frames.caption: RETURN count=2: 3 + 1 = 4.
frames.note: Finish this frame’s pending work, then return its answer to the next caller. Answers flow back in reverse call order because the most recent unfinished caller resumes first.

frames.caption: RESUME count=3: the child returned 4; assign smaller=4.
frames.note: The child frame has left the stack. Execution continues in its immediate caller at the suspended assignment; it does not jump straight to the first call. This caller still has its own addition to do.

frames.caption: RETURN count=3: 4 + 4 = 8.
frames.note: Finish this frame’s pending work, then return its answer to the next caller. Answers flow back in reverse call order because the most recent unfinished caller resumes first.

frames.caption: RESUME count=4: the child returned 8; assign smaller=8.
frames.note: The child frame has left the stack. Execution continues in its immediate caller at the suspended assignment; it does not jump straight to the first call. This caller still has its own addition to do.

frames.caption: RETURN count=4: 8 + 2 = 10.
frames.note: Finish this frame’s pending work, then return its answer to the next caller. Answers flow back in reverse call order because the most recent unfinished caller resumes first.

frames.caption: DONE: sum = 10. All calls returned; no pending work remains.
frames.note: Four additions, five calls, and a maximum of five live frames. For n items this is O(n) time and O(n) stack space. The lesson is the call lifecycle, not an efficient way to sum: a loop would avoid the growing call stack.
